Ideal for meetings, interviews, call center recordings, and large-scale content processing pipelines. Supports files up to 2 hours long Advanced transcription and translation Speaker diarization and timestamp support Note: You can upload up to 20 audio files per job. Model Availability: The Batch API supports Saaras v3 with multiple output modes via the mode parameter. Using saaras:v4 ? Pass a keyterms list inside job_parameters to bias recognition toward specific names, places, brands, or technical terms. See Keyterm Prompting . Supported Modes (Saaras v3) Mode Description Output transcribe Standard transcription in the original language Text in source language translate Transcribe and translate to English English text verbatim Word-for-word transcription including filler words and repetitions Verbatim text in source language translit Transcribe and transliterate to Roman script Romanized text codemix Transcribe code-mixed speech (e.g., Hindi-English) naturally Code-mixed text Features Processing Supports up to 2 hours audio Synchronous and asynchronous job-based API Upload multiple files per job Audio &amp; Language Support Indian languages and English Automatic language detection Diarization and timestamp support Timestamps Chunk-level timestamps only (not word-level) Each chunk covers a sentence or phrase segment Provides start and end times for each chunk of text Useful for subtitle alignment and audio navigation Speaker Diarization Identify multiple speakers Output includes speaker labels (SPEAKER_00, etc.) Ideal for meetings and interviews Word-level timestamps are not supported. The Batch API returns chunk-level timestamps only. Each timestamp entry covers a sentence or phrase, not an individual word. If your use case requires per-word timing, this is not currently available. Input audio codec (batch) When you call init job ( POST /speech-to-text/job/v1 ), set input_audio_codec inside job_parameters when needed. Behavior matches the REST upload APIs: most formats are auto-detected; for raw PCM ( pcm_s16le , pcm_l16 , pcm_raw ) you must set this field. PCM must be 16 kHz sample rate. See supported formats and MIME types for the full list. Use the same field on speech-to-text translate bulk jobs when translate job parameters include input_audio_codec . Python JavaScript # input_audio_codec is set via the low-level init-job API job = client . speech_to_text_job . initialise ( job_parameters = { &quot; model &quot; : &quot; saaras:v4 &quot; , &quot; mode &quot; : &quot; transcribe &quot; , &quot; language_code &quot; : &quot; hi-IN &quot; , &quot; input_audio_codec &quot; : &quot; pcm_s16le &quot; , # required for raw PCM uploads in the batch }, ) Code Examples Choosing a Mode To switch between modes, simply change the mode parameter in your job creation call. The rest of the workflow (upload, start, wait, download) remains the same. Transcribe Translate Verbatim Translit Codemix Transcribe audio in the original language. Python JavaScript job = client . speech_to_text_job . create_job ( model = &quot; saaras:v4 &quot; , mode = &quot; transcribe &quot; , # Standard transcription language_code = &quot; hi-IN &quot; , with_diarization = True , num_speakers = 2 , ) REST download note If you call Batch - Download Results ( POST /speech-to-text/job/v1/download-files ) directly, the body must include both job_id and a files array (for example [&quot;0.json&quot;] ). Output filenames come from the Batch - Get Status response ( job_details[].outputs[].file_name ). The SDK download_outputs() method supplies these automatically. Full Example Once you’ve created a job with your chosen mode, the upload, processing, and download workflow is the same for all modes: Python (Sync) Python (Async) JavaScript from sarvamai import SarvamAI def main (): client = SarvamAI ( api_subscription_key = &quot; YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY &quot; ) # Create batch job: change mode as needed job = client . speech_to_text_job . create_job ( model = &quot; saaras:v4 &quot; , mode = &quot; transcribe &quot; , language_code = &quot; en-IN &quot; , with_diarization = True , num_speakers = 2 ) # Upload and process files audio_paths = [ &quot; path/to/audio1.mp3 &quot; , &quot; path/to/audio2.mp3 &quot; ] job . upload_files ( file_paths = audio_paths ) job . start () # Wait for completion job . wait_until_complete () # Check file-level results file_results = job . get_file_results () print ( f &quot; \n Successful: { len ( file_results [ &#x27; successful &#x27; ]) } &quot; ) for f in file_results [ &#x27; successful &#x27; ]: print ( f &quot; ✓ { f [ &#x27; file_name &#x27; ] } &quot; ) print ( f &quot; \n Failed: { len ( file_results [ &#x27; failed &#x27; ]) } &quot; ) for f in file_results [ &#x27; failed &#x27; ]: print ( f &quot; ✗ { f [ &#x27; file_name &#x27; ] } : { f [ &#x27; error_message &#x27; ] } &quot; ) # Download outputs for successful files if file_results [ &#x27; successful &#x27; ]: job . download_outputs ( output_dir = &quot; ./output &quot; ) print ( f &quot; \n Downloaded { len ( file_results [ &#x27; successful &#x27; ]) } file(s) to: ./output&quot; ) if __name__ == &quot; __main__ &quot; : main () Speaker Diarization Speaker diarization automatically identifies and separates different speakers in an audio recording. This feature is ideal for meetings, interviews, and multi-speaker conversations where you need to know who said what. Capabilities Identify multiple speakers in a single audio file Assign unique speaker IDs (speaker 1, speaker 2, etc.) Provide timestamps for each speaker segment Works with up to 20 speakers per audio file Output Format When with_diarization=True is passed in the request, the response includes a diarized_transcript field with detailed speaker information: { &quot; request_id &quot; : &quot; 20260130_d8d2c0e6-1eb6-4982-8045-b267d5165c44 &quot; , &quot; transcript &quot; : &quot; Full transcript text... &quot; , &quot; timestamps &quot; : { &quot; chunks &quot; : [ &quot; Hello, how can I help you today? &quot; , &quot; I have a question. &quot; ] , &quot; start_time_seconds &quot; : [ 0.01 , 2.8 ] , &quot; end_time_seconds &quot; : [ 2.5 , 4.2 ] } , &quot; diarized_transcript &quot; : { &quot; entries &quot; : [ { &quot; transcript &quot; : &quot; Hello, how can I help you today? &quot; , &quot; start_time_seconds &quot; : 0.01 , &quot; end_time_seconds &quot; : 2.5 , &quot; speaker_id &quot; : &quot; 0 &quot; } , { &quot; transcript &quot; : &quot; I have a question. &quot; , &quot; start_time_seconds &quot; : 2.8 , &quot; end_time_seconds &quot; : 4.2 , &quot; speaker_id &quot; : &quot; 1 &quot; } ] } , &quot; language_code &quot; : &quot; en-IN &quot; } Each entry contains: transcript : The text spoken by the speaker start_time_seconds : When the speaker started speaking (float) end_time_seconds : When the speaker stopped speaking (float) speaker_id : Unique identifier for the speaker (e.g., “0”, “1”) The SarvamAI SDK supports both synchronous and asynchronous programming in Python. This refers to how your code interacts with the SDK, not how the server handles the processing of requests. Polling Defaults job.wait_until_complete() polls GET /speech-to-text/job/v1/{job_id}/status in a loop until the job reaches a terminal state: def wait_until_complete ( self , poll_interval : int = 5 , timeout : int = 600 ) -&gt; JobStatusResponse Parameter Default Meaning poll_interval 5 seconds Time between status checks timeout 600 seconds (10 minutes) Raises TimeoutError if the job hasn’t reached Completed / Failed by then Both are overridable, for example job.wait_until_complete(poll_interval=10, timeout=1800) , if your files are large enough that 10 minutes isn’t enough headroom. The legacy document_intelligence API’s wait_until_complete() uses different defaults (2-second poll interval, no timeout by default). Its successor, Document AI , has no such helper. You poll get_status() yourself. Webhook Support For long-running batch jobs, you can use webhooks to receive notifications when jobs complete instead of polling for status updates. Setting Up Webhooks When creating a job, include a callback parameter with your webhook URL and authentication token: Python (Async) Python (Sync) from sarvamai import AsyncSarvamAI , BulkJobCallbackParams client = AsyncSarvamAI ( api_subscription_key = &quot; YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY &quot; ) job = await client . speech_to_text_job . create_job ( model = &quot; saaras:v4 &quot; , mode = &quot; transcribe &quot; , with_diarization = True , callback = BulkJobCallbackParams ( url = &quot; https://your-server.com/webhook-endpoint &quot; , auth_token = &quot; your-secret-token &quot; ) ) Webhook Payload When a job finishes (or fails), Sarvam AI sends a POST to your callback URL. The body matches the same JobStatusResponse schema returned by GET /speech-to-text/job/v1/{job_id}/status . It is a status notification , not the transcript text itself. Sarvam includes your auth_token in the X-SARVAM-JOB-CALLBACK-TOKEN request header (validate this on every request). { &quot; job_id &quot; : &quot; job_12345 &quot; , &quot; job_state &quot; : &quot; Completed &quot; , &quot; created_at &quot; : &quot; 2026-05-27T10:30:00Z &quot; , &quot; updated_at &quot; : &quot; 2026-05-27T10:35:12Z &quot; , &quot; total_files &quot; : 2 , &quot; successful_files_count &quot; : 2 , &quot; failed_files_count &quot; : 0 , &quot; storage_container_type &quot; : &quot; Azure &quot; , &quot; error_message &quot; : &quot;&quot; , &quot; job_details &quot; : [ { &quot; inputs &quot; : [{ &quot; file_name &quot; : &quot; meeting.mp3 &quot; , &quot; file_id &quot; : &quot; input-0 &quot; }] , &quot; outputs &quot; : [{ &quot; file_name &quot; : &quot; 0.json &quot; , &quot; file_id &quot; : &quot; output-0 &quot; }] , &quot; state &quot; : &quot; Success &quot; , &quot; error_message &quot; : null , &quot; exception_name &quot; : null } ] } Field Meaning job_state One of Accepted , Pending , Running , Completed , or Failed (title case) job_details Per-file status: input/output file names, processing state , and errors successful_files_count / failed_files_count How many files succeeded vs failed Transcripts are not in the webhook. Each successful file’s transcript lives in a downloaded JSON (for example 0.json listed under job_details[].outputs ). After job_state is Completed , call POST /speech-to-text/job/v1/download-files (or use job.download_outputs() in the SDK) and parse those files. See Speaker Diarization → Output Format for the JSON shape ( transcript , language_code , optional diarized_transcript , etc.). Webhook Server Example Here’s a simple FastAPI server to handle webhook callbacks: from fastapi import FastAPI , Request , HTTPException import uvicorn app = FastAPI () VALID_TOKEN = &quot; your-secret-token &quot; @ app . post ( &quot; /webhook-endpoint &quot; ) async def handle_webhook ( request : Request ): # Validate authentication token = request . headers . get ( &quot; X-SARVAM-JOB-CALLBACK-TOKEN &quot; ) if token != VALID_TOKEN : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 403 , detail = &quot; Invalid token &quot; ) # Process the webhook data data = await request . json () job_id = data . get ( &quot; job_id &quot; ) job_state = data . get ( &quot; job_state &quot; ) if job_state == &quot; Completed &quot; : print ( f &quot;Job { job_id } completed successfully!&quot; ) # Fetch transcripts: download output JSON files (see job_details[].outputs) elif job_state == &quot; Failed &quot; : print ( f &quot;Job { job_id } failed: { data . get ( &#x27; error_message &#x27; ) } &quot; ) # Handle failure return { &quot; status &quot; : &quot; success &quot; } if __name__ == &quot; __main__ &quot; : uvicorn . run ( app , host = &quot; 0.0.0.0 &quot; , port = 8000 ) Your webhook server must respond with a 200 status code within 30 seconds. Make sure your webhook URL is publicly accessible and uses HTTPS in production. Ideal for meetings, interviews, call center recordings, and\n large-scale content processing pipelines.\n\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cul\u003e\n \u003cli\u003e\n Supports files up to 2 hours long\n \u003c/li\u003e\n\n \u003cli\u003e\n Advanced transcription and translation\n \u003c/li\u003e\n\n \u003cli\u003e\n Speaker diarization and timestamp support\n \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003e\n \u003cstrong\u003eNote:\u003c/strong\u003e You can upload up to \u003ccode\u003e20\u003c/code\u003e audio files per\n job.\n\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n **Model Availability:** The Batch API supports **Saaras v3** with multiple output modes via the `mode` parameter.\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n\u003cTip\u003e\n Using `saaras:v4`? Pass a `keyterms` list inside `job_parameters` to bias recognition toward specific names, places, brands, or technical terms. See [Keyterm Prompting](/api/api-guides-tutorials/speech-to-text/how-to/keyterms).\n\u003c/Tip\u003e\n\n### Supported Modes (Saaras v3)\n\n| Mode | Description | Output |\n| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |\n| `transcribe` | Standard transcription in the original language | Text in source language |\n| `translate` | Transcribe and translate to English | English text |\n| `verbatim` | Word-for-word transcription including filler words and repetitions | Verbatim text in source language |\n| `translit` | Transcribe and transliterate to Roman script | Romanized text |\n| `codemix` | Transcribe code-mixed speech (e.g., Hindi-English) naturally | Code-mixed text |\n\n## Features\n\n\u003cCardGroup cols={2}\u003e\n \u003cCard title=\"Processing\"\u003e\n * Supports up to 2 hours audio\n * Synchronous and asynchronous job-based API\n * Upload multiple files per job\n \u003c/Card\u003e\n\n {\" \"}\n\n \u003cCard title=\"Audio \u0026 Language Support\"\u003e\n * Indian languages and English\n * Automatic language detection\n * Diarization and timestamp support\n \u003c/Card\u003e\n\n \u003cCard title=\"Timestamps\"\u003e\n * **Chunk-level** timestamps only (not word-level)\n * Each chunk covers a sentence or phrase segment\n * Provides start and end times for each chunk of text\n * Useful for subtitle alignment and audio navigation\n \u003c/Card\u003e\n\n \u003cCard title=\"Speaker Diarization\"\u003e\n * Identify multiple speakers\n * Output includes speaker labels (SPEAKER\\_00, etc.)\n * Ideal for meetings and interviews\n \u003c/Card\u003e\n\u003c/CardGroup\u003e\n\n\u003cWarning\u003e\n **Word-level timestamps are not supported.** The Batch API returns **chunk-level** timestamps only. Each timestamp entry covers a sentence or phrase, not an individual word. If your use case requires per-word timing, this is not currently available.\n\u003c/Warning\u003e\n\n## Input audio codec (batch)\n\nWhen you call **init job** (`POST /speech-to-text/job/v1`), set `input_audio_codec` inside `job_parameters` when needed. Behavior matches the REST upload APIs: most formats are auto-detected; for **raw PCM** (`pcm_s16le`, `pcm_l16`, `pcm_raw`) you **must** set this field. PCM must be **16 kHz** sample rate. See [supported formats and MIME types](/api/api-guides-tutorials/speech-to-text/overview) for the full list.\n\nUse the same field on **speech-to-text translate** bulk jobs when translate job parameters include `input_audio_codec`.\n\n\u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python\" active\u003e\n ```python\n # input_audio_codec is set via the low-level init-job API\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.initialise(\n job_parameters={\n \"model\": \"saaras:v4\",\n \"mode\": \"transcribe\",\n \"language_code\": \"hi-IN\",\n \"input_audio_codec\": \"pcm_s16le\", # required for raw PCM uploads in the batch\n },\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n // input_audio_codec is set via the low-level init-job API\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.initialise({\n job_parameters: {\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"transcribe\",\n language_code: \"hi-IN\",\n input_audio_codec: \"pcm_s16le\",\n },\n });\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n\n## Code Examples\n\n### Choosing a Mode\n\nTo switch between modes, simply change the `mode` parameter in your job creation call. The rest of the workflow (upload, start, wait, download) remains the same.\n\n\u003cTabs\u003e\n \u003cTab title=\"Transcribe\"\u003e\n Transcribe audio in the original language.\n\n \u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python\" active\u003e\n ```python\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"transcribe\", # Standard transcription\n language_code=\"hi-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2,\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.createJob({\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"transcribe\", // Standard transcription\n languageCode: \"hi-IN\",\n withDiarization: true,\n numSpeakers: 2,\n });\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n \u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n \u003c/Tab\u003e\n\n \u003cTab title=\"Translate\"\u003e\n Transcribe and translate audio to English.\n\n \u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python\" active\u003e\n ```python\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"translate\", # Translate to English\n language_code=\"hi-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2,\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.createJob({\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"translate\", // Translate to English\n languageCode: \"hi-IN\",\n withDiarization: true,\n numSpeakers: 2,\n });\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n \u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n \u003c/Tab\u003e\n\n \u003cTab title=\"Verbatim\"\u003e\n Word-for-word transcription including filler words and repetitions.\n\n \u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python\" active\u003e\n ```python\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"verbatim\", # Include fillers \u0026 repetitions\n language_code=\"hi-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2,\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.createJob({\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"verbatim\", // Include fillers \u0026 repetitions\n languageCode: \"hi-IN\",\n withDiarization: true,\n numSpeakers: 2,\n });\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n \u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n \u003c/Tab\u003e\n\n \u003cTab title=\"Translit\"\u003e\n Transcribe and transliterate to Roman script.\n\n \u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python\" active\u003e\n ```python\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"translit\", # Romanized output\n language_code=\"hi-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2,\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.createJob({\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"translit\", // Romanized output\n languageCode: \"hi-IN\",\n withDiarization: true,\n numSpeakers: 2,\n });\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n \u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n \u003c/Tab\u003e\n\n \u003cTab title=\"Codemix\"\u003e\n Transcribe code-mixed speech (e.g., Hindi-English) naturally.\n\n \u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python\" active\u003e\n ```python\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"codemix\", # Handle mixed-language speech\n language_code=\"hi-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2,\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.createJob({\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"codemix\", // Handle mixed-language speech\n languageCode: \"hi-IN\",\n withDiarization: true,\n numSpeakers: 2,\n });\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n \u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n \u003c/Tab\u003e\n\u003c/Tabs\u003e\n\n### REST download note\n\nIf you call **Batch - Download Results** (`POST /speech-to-text/job/v1/download-files`) directly, the body must include both `job_id` and a `files` array (for example `[\"0.json\"]`). Output filenames come from the [Batch - Get Status](/api/api-guides-tutorials/speech-to-text/batch-api) response (`job_details[].outputs[].file_name`). The SDK `download_outputs()` method supplies these automatically.\n\n### Full Example\n\nOnce you've created a job with your chosen mode, the upload, processing, and download workflow is the same for all modes:\n\n\u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python (Sync)\" active\u003e\n ```python\n from sarvamai import SarvamAI\n\n def main():\n client = SarvamAI(api_subscription_key=\"YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY\")\n\n # Create batch job: change mode as needed\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"transcribe\",\n language_code=\"en-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2\n )\n\n # Upload and process files\n audio_paths = [\"path/to/audio1.mp3\", \"path/to/audio2.mp3\"]\n job.upload_files(file_paths=audio_paths)\n job.start()\n\n # Wait for completion\n job.wait_until_complete()\n\n # Check file-level results\n file_results = job.get_file_results()\n\n print(f\"\\nSuccessful: {len(file_results['successful'])}\")\n for f in file_results['successful']:\n print(f\" ✓ {f['file_name']}\")\n\n print(f\"\\nFailed: {len(file_results['failed'])}\")\n for f in file_results['failed']:\n print(f\" ✗ {f['file_name']}: {f['error_message']}\")\n\n # Download outputs for successful files\n if file_results['successful']:\n job.download_outputs(output_dir=\"./output\")\n print(f\"\\nDownloaded {len(file_results['successful'])} file(s) to: ./output\")\n\n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n main()\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python (Async)\"\u003e\n ```python\n import asyncio\n from sarvamai import AsyncSarvamAI\n\n async def main():\n client = AsyncSarvamAI(api_subscription_key=\"YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY\")\n\n # Create batch job: change mode as needed\n job = await client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"transcribe\",\n language_code=\"en-IN\",\n with_diarization=True,\n num_speakers=2\n )\n\n # Upload and process files\n audio_paths = [\"path/to/audio1.mp3\", \"path/to/audio2.mp3\"]\n await job.upload_files(file_paths=audio_paths)\n await job.start()\n\n # Wait for completion\n await job.wait_until_complete()\n\n # Check file-level results\n file_results = await job.get_file_results()\n\n print(f\"\\nSuccessful: {len(file_results['successful'])}\")\n for f in file_results['successful']:\n print(f\" ✓ {f['file_name']}\")\n\n print(f\"\\nFailed: {len(file_results['failed'])}\")\n for f in file_results['failed']:\n print(f\" ✗ {f['file_name']}: {f['error_message']}\")\n\n # Download outputs for successful files\n if file_results['successful']:\n await job.download_outputs(output_dir=\"./output\")\n print(f\"\\nDownloaded {len(file_results['successful'])} file(s) to: ./output\")\n\n if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n asyncio.run(main())\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"JavaScript\"\u003e\n ```javascript\n import { SarvamAIClient } from \"sarvamai\";\n\n async function main() {\n const client = new SarvamAIClient({\n apiSubscriptionKey: \"YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY\"\n });\n\n // Create batch job, change mode as needed\n const job = await client.speechToTextJob.createJob({\n model: \"saaras:v4\",\n mode: \"transcribe\",\n languageCode: \"en-IN\",\n withDiarization: true,\n numSpeakers: 2\n });\n\n // Upload and process files\n const audioPaths = [\"path/to/audio1.mp3\", \"path/to/audio2.mp3\"];\n await job.uploadFiles(audioPaths);\n await job.start();\n\n // Wait for completion\n await job.waitUntilComplete();\n\n // Check file-level results\n const fileResults = await job.getFileResults();\n\n console.log(`\\nSuccessful: ${fileResults.successful.length}`);\n for (const f of fileResults.successful) {\n console.log(` ✓ ${f.file_name}`);\n }\n\n console.log(`\\nFailed: ${fileResults.failed.length}`);\n for (const f of fileResults.failed) {\n console.log(` ✗ ${f.file_name}: ${f.error_message}`);\n }\n\n // Download outputs for successful files\n if (fileResults.successful.length \u003e 0) {\n await job.downloadOutputs(\"./output\");\n console.log(`\\nDownloaded ${fileResults.successful.length} file(s) to: ./output`);\n }\n }\n\n main().catch(console.error);\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n\n## Speaker Diarization\n\nSpeaker diarization automatically identifies and separates different speakers in an audio recording. This feature is ideal for meetings, interviews, and multi-speaker conversations where you need to know who said what.\n\n### Capabilities\n\n* Identify multiple speakers in a single audio file\n* Assign unique speaker IDs (speaker 1, speaker 2, etc.)\n* Provide timestamps for each speaker segment\n* Works with up to 20 speakers per audio file\n\n### Output Format\n\nWhen `with_diarization=True` is passed in the request, the response includes a `diarized_transcript` field with detailed speaker information:\n\n```json\n{\n \"request_id\": \"20260130_d8d2c0e6-1eb6-4982-8045-b267d5165c44\",\n \"transcript\": \"Full transcript text...\",\n \"timestamps\": {\n \"chunks\": [\"Hello, how can I help you today?\", \"I have a question.\"],\n \"start_time_seconds\": [0.01, 2.8],\n \"end_time_seconds\": [2.5, 4.2]\n },\n \"diarized_transcript\": {\n \"entries\": [\n {\n \"transcript\": \"Hello, how can I help you today?\",\n \"start_time_seconds\": 0.01,\n \"end_time_seconds\": 2.5,\n \"speaker_id\": \"0\"\n },\n {\n \"transcript\": \"I have a question.\",\n \"start_time_seconds\": 2.8,\n \"end_time_seconds\": 4.2,\n \"speaker_id\": \"1\"\n }\n ]\n },\n \"language_code\": \"en-IN\"\n}\n```\n\nEach entry contains:\n\n* `transcript`: The text spoken by the speaker\n* `start_time_seconds`: When the speaker started speaking (float)\n* `end_time_seconds`: When the speaker stopped speaking (float)\n* `speaker_id`: Unique identifier for the speaker (e.g., \"0\", \"1\")\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n The SarvamAI SDK supports both synchronous and asynchronous programming in\n Python. This refers to how your code interacts with the SDK, not how the\n server handles the processing of requests.\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n## Polling Defaults\n\n`job.wait_until_complete()` polls `GET /speech-to-text/job/v1/{job_id}/status` in a loop until the job reaches a terminal state:\n\n```python\ndef wait_until_complete(self, poll_interval: int = 5, timeout: int = 600) -\u003e JobStatusResponse\n```\n\n| Parameter | Default | Meaning |\n| --------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `poll_interval` | **5 seconds** | Time between status checks |\n| `timeout` | **600 seconds** (10 minutes) | Raises `TimeoutError` if the job hasn't reached `Completed`/`Failed` by then |\n\nBoth are overridable, for example `job.wait_until_complete(poll_interval=10, timeout=1800)`, if your files are large enough that 10 minutes isn't enough headroom.\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n The legacy `document_intelligence` API's `wait_until_complete()` uses different defaults (2-second poll interval, no timeout by default). Its successor, [Document AI](/api/api-guides-tutorials/document-intelligence/overview), has no such helper. You poll `get_status()` yourself.\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n## Webhook Support\n\nFor long-running batch jobs, you can use webhooks to receive notifications when jobs complete instead of polling for status updates.\n\n### Setting Up Webhooks\n\nWhen creating a job, include a `callback` parameter with your webhook URL and authentication token:\n\n\u003cCodeGroup\u003e\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python (Async)\" active\u003e\n ```python\n from sarvamai import AsyncSarvamAI, BulkJobCallbackParams\n\n client = AsyncSarvamAI(api_subscription_key=\"YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY\")\n\n job = await client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"transcribe\",\n with_diarization=True,\n callback=BulkJobCallbackParams(\n url=\"https://your-server.com/webhook-endpoint\",\n auth_token=\"your-secret-token\"\n )\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\n \u003cCodeBlock title=\"Python (Sync)\"\u003e\n ```python\n from sarvamai import SarvamAI, BulkJobCallbackParams\n\n client = SarvamAI(api_subscription_key=\"YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY\")\n\n job = client.speech_to_text_job.create_job(\n model=\"saaras:v4\",\n mode=\"transcribe\",\n with_diarization=True,\n callback=BulkJobCallbackParams(\n url=\"https://your-server.com/webhook-endpoint\",\n auth_token=\"your-secret-token\"\n )\n )\n ```\n \u003c/CodeBlock\u003e\n\u003c/CodeGroup\u003e\n\n### Webhook Payload\n\nWhen a job finishes (or fails), Sarvam AI sends a **POST** to your callback URL. The body matches the same `JobStatusResponse` schema returned by [`GET /speech-to-text/job/v1/{job_id}/status`](/api-reference/speech-to-text/stt/job/status). It is a **status notification**, not the transcript text itself.\n\nSarvam includes your `auth_token` in the **`X-SARVAM-JOB-CALLBACK-TOKEN`** request header (validate this on every request).\n\n```json\n{\n \"job_id\": \"job_12345\",\n \"job_state\": \"Completed\",\n \"created_at\": \"2026-05-27T10:30:00Z\",\n \"updated_at\": \"2026-05-27T10:35:12Z\",\n \"total_files\": 2,\n \"successful_files_count\": 2,\n \"failed_files_count\": 0,\n \"storage_container_type\": \"Azure\",\n \"error_message\": \"\",\n \"job_details\": [\n {\n \"inputs\": [{ \"file_name\": \"meeting.mp3\", \"file_id\": \"input-0\" }],\n \"outputs\": [{ \"file_name\": \"0.json\", \"file_id\": \"output-0\" }],\n \"state\": \"Success\",\n \"error_message\": null,\n \"exception_name\": null\n }\n ]\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `job_state` | One of `Accepted`, `Pending`, `Running`, `Completed`, or `Failed` (title case) |\n| `job_details` | Per-file status: input/output file names, processing `state`, and errors |\n| `successful_files_count` / `failed_files_count` | How many files succeeded vs failed |\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n **Transcripts are not in the webhook.** Each successful file's transcript lives in a **downloaded JSON** (for example `0.json` listed under `job_details[].outputs`). After `job_state` is `Completed`, call [`POST /speech-to-text/job/v1/download-files`](/api-reference/speech-to-text/stt/job/download) (or use `job.download_outputs()` in the SDK) and parse those files. See [Speaker Diarization → Output Format](#speaker-diarization) for the JSON shape (`transcript`, `language_code`, optional `diarized_transcript`, etc.).\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n### Webhook Server Example\n\nHere's a simple FastAPI server to handle webhook callbacks:\n\n```python\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException\nimport uvicorn\n\napp = FastAPI()\nVALID_TOKEN = \"your-secret-token\"\n\n@app.post(\"/webhook-endpoint\")\nasync def handle_webhook(request: Request):\n # Validate authentication\n token = request.headers.get(\"X-SARVAM-JOB-CALLBACK-TOKEN\")\n if token != VALID_TOKEN:\n raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid token\")\n \n # Process the webhook data\n data = await request.json()\n job_id = data.get(\"job_id\")\n job_state = data.get(\"job_state\")\n \n if job_state == \"Completed\":\n print(f\"Job {job_id} completed successfully!\")\n # Fetch transcripts: download output JSON files (see job_details[].outputs)\n elif job_state == \"Failed\":\n print(f\"Job {job_id} failed: {data.get('error_message')}\")\n # Handle failure\n \n return {\"status\": \"success\"}\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n uvicorn.run(app, host=\"0.0.0.0\", port=8000)\n```\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n Your webhook server must respond with a 200 status code within 30 seconds.\n Make sure your webhook URL is publicly accessible and uses HTTPS in production.\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n## Next Steps\n\n\u003cSteps\u003e\n \u003cStep title=\"Choose Your API\"\u003e\n Select the appropriate API type based on your use case.\n \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n \u003cStep title=\"Get API Key\"\u003e\n Sign up and get your API key from the\n [dashboard](https://dashboard.sarvam.ai).\n \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n \u003cStep title=\"Go Live\"\u003e\n Deploy your integration and monitor usage in the dashboard.\n \u003c/Step\u003e\n\u003c/Steps\u003e\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n Need help choosing the right API?
